text: Side Story: Eunie (Japanese: , Saido Sutōrī Yūni) is an Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Eunie.
Side Story: Lanz (Japanese: , Saido Sutōrī Rantsu) is a Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Lanz.
Side Story: Taion (Japanese: , Saido Sutōrī Taion) is a Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Taion.

Side Story: Mio (Japanese: , Saido Sutōrī Mio) is an Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Mio. Miyabi is unlocked as a Hero upon completion of the quest. Completing this quest is required to progress in the story.
Side Story: Sena (Japanese: , Saido Sutōrī Sena) is an Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Sena.
Snow Conches are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Battlescar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Silverseeds are Seed Collectibles in and . They can be found in the Pentelas Region in . They can also be purchased from the Colony Lambda Caravan, or produced from the Clifftop Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Aurora Shelf in .
Smushi Rices are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. It can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan, or produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Smalnuts are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be purchased from the Colony 30 Caravan, or produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Skelter Medoozes are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Medooz family, and can be found at level 27-28 at at Fallfoot Battlescar near the base of the Great Cotte Falls. One is fought at level 70 during the first wave of the Challenge Battle Men! Of! The Sea! IV.
Sniper Rhoguls are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 35-36 at High Maktha Wildwood in the Pentelas Region.

Sickle Cricket Fossils are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced by the Tableland Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They are fossilized Sickle Crickets from the Kingdom of Uraya.
Skyclams are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be purchased from the O'Virbus Caravan for 1665 G, or produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Silent Turbines are Collectible items in . They can be found in Swordmarch. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.
Silver Ravoon Bones are items in and . They are dropped by Ravoons.
Slender Flamii Bones are items in . They can be dropped by Biban Flamii which can be found near the Hargan Point Camp.
Skeeter Honeys are items in . They can be obtained from the Skeeter family of enemies. The rare variant can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan.
Silent Vangs are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 42-43 in the Great Sword Passage within the Great Sword's Base.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Silver Braided Belts are Accessories in and .
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Silver Chokers are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be acquired from Keen Chicky-Chicky.

Snow-White Mythrice is a Key Item in . It is obtained from the Lambda Commissary in Colony Lambda during Inhumanity so Sena can make Onigiri for Segiri. More Snow-White Mythrice is obtained from the Ecto Hollow after No. 13 escapes during Invisible Bond. Sena and Segiri use it to make some Onigiri for the rest of Colony 0.
The Sinister Faceplate is a Key Item in . It is found on the Distant Fingertip on Elaice Highway. It is needed to complete Writer's Block.
Silky White Sashes are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region and obtained from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Sniper Ansels are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found at level 45-46 on the Urayan Trail.
Smart Ansels are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found at level 23 in the Dannagh Desert.
Shuvai Merfreys are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Merfrey family, and can be found at level 46 in Erythia Sea.
Shut-In is a Standard Quest in . Segiri must be in the party.

Six Angry Beasts is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will unlock the Swimwear A outfit for Taion.
Silver Gauntlets are DLC Accessories in . They can be purchased from Prize X-change Red in the Land of Challenge for 6000 Noponstones.

Silver Cyclone (Japanese: , Shirubāsaikuron) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Null Slash that can only be used by Ethel. She does a downward slash, then two hopping circular slashes, then an upward slash and finishes with a spreading slash.

Snake Eyes is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It can be upgraded by fulfilling the condition of "Defeat the indicated monster(s): 15 Hazardous Jarrahed". It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Hazardous Jarrahed while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Slow Recharge is a Status Effect in and . It reduces the character's recharge rate; Keves (and enemy) cooldown timers will tick slower, Agnus arts will gain less charge per auto-attack or Art cancel, and Talent Arts will gain less charge upon a Role Action.
Simmertree are Wood Collectibles in . They can be found in Vermilion Woods. Three are needed for the Vermilion Woods Collectopaedia.
Smart Bomb is one of Nikol's arts in . It becomes unlockable upon defeating the Ritteli Rhinon at the Echoes of Gran Dell Citadel.
Skarn Volffs are two Bosses in . They are members of the Volff family that are fought at level 16 on the Aurora Shelf. Glimmer fights them alone.
Skewers Recipe is a Key Item in . It allows the party to cook Game Skewers at Rest Spots. It is obtained upon completing Elevator Repairs.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Silver Jewels are Accessories in .
Smackdown Brannigan (Japanese: , Kyōshū no Baranasu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 24 at the bottom of Tephra Hill in Yesterdale.
Sniper Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 30 at Raguel Lake on The Ragmos Desolation.
Smothering Andante (Japanese: , Yokusei no Andante) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Ardun family, and can be found at level 11 at the Gaur Viaduct on the Aurora Shelf.
Skyward Slash (Japanese: , Kokūzan, "Empty Sky Slash") is a Battle Art in . It is one of Jin's arts as a temporary party member.
Sky Sunder is one of Ga Jiarg's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn it by completing A Challenger Approaches.

Skell Armor is defensive Skell Gear in and . It is similar to ground armor in that it provides protection to a Skell. Unlike ground armor, changing skell armor does not change the skell's appearance. Thus, there is no Fashion Gear for skell armor.
Snipers are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
Skell Fuel Recovery is a buff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Skell Fuel steadily increases; does not affect parked Skells.
Shynini is an NPC in . Shynini is a Nopon who can be found at the Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild. Shynini runs a shop called Shynini's Accessories.

Snikisniki (Japanese: , Kagege) is an NPC in . Snikisniki is a Nopon who can be found at the Bower Lounge in the Argentum Trade Guild. He is involved in the quest Hide and Seek where he must be found along with Aft and Talulu.

The Sly Krabble (Japanese: , Gottsun Kuraibu) is a Quest Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Krabble family found at level 2 after Salvaging on the Salvage Deck of the Argentum Trade Guild during Better Late Than Never. This enemy only drops the Keepsake Necklace Key Item.

Soldier Arachnos (Japanese: , Sorujā Supaido) are story exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and appear only during the boss fight with the Arachno Queen. Soldier Arachnos do not drop Treasure Chests.

Soft Sea Cucumbers (Japanese: , Funyafunyamako) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they are tropic-dwelling sea cucumbers and their softness make them hard to catch. Four are required for Honouring the Nopon Sage.
Sonia (Japanese: ) is a Homs in . She can be found in the southern portion of the Commercial District in Colony 9.

The Solidum Telethia (Japanese: , Soridumu Tereshia) is a boss in . It is a Licorne-type Telethia, and is fought alongside Tyrea in the Ceremony Hall in the High Entia Tomb. It does not carry or drop any treasure.

Sour Turnips (Japanese: , Shibu Kōrurabi, Bitter Kohlrabi) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are more astringent than sour and they are considered tasty in some regions. Three are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 13,200 Noponstones.

Spicy Cabbages (Japanese: , Hotto Kyabeshi) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are packed with nutrients, but they are tricky to prepare properly as they are complex vegetables.

The Sparkling Pool (Japanese: , Kirakira-ike) is a Secret Area in . It is located in Makna Forest. It can be reached by climbing a large tree root from the water at the Eks Watering Hole to higher ground and continuing south. The pool normally has two collectables, except at dawn, from 05:00 to 06:00, when an additional eight collectables appear. When swimming in the pool, a slight continuous clink is heard anytime, except at dawn, indicating that something may appear at the right time.

Sour Gooseberries (Japanese: , Shāpu Kuranberi, Sharp Cranberry) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are bitter fruit from which prairie trees sprout and grating them create a green dye. Four are required for A Dash of Colour.
Sorrow Beetles (Japanese: , Fumankanabun) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 9. According to their description, they are frustrated-looking beetles mostly found near water.

Spicy Nuts (Japanese: , Piritto Nashi, Spicy Pear) are collectables in . They can be found in Frontier Village. According to their description, they are a little sweet, but spicy on the tongue, and also irresistibly stimulating.
Soil Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Flattened Flowers.

Spiral Lamps (Japanese: , Rasenranpu) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in the High Entia Tomb. According to their description, they are helical lamps with nasty cracks and there is no point trying to fix them. Two are required for the Timed Quest Collection Quest 4 at Alcamoth.

Spicy Papayas (Japanese: , Hotto Papaiya) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they warm someone's body to the core and they are good for poor circulation. Five are required for Nopon Determination.

Snow Transistors (Japanese: , Sunō Toranjisuta) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are transistors that cause visions of snow flurries when turned on.
The Spark Lancer (Japanese: , Supākuransā) is a weapon in . It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.
The Soldier Pike (Japanese: , Sorujāpaiku) is a weapon in . It is one of Reyn's gunlances. It is not effective against Mechon. It can be dropped by various enemies in Colony 9.
Sonic Lancers (Japanese: , Sonikkuransā) are weapons in . They are Reyn's gunlances, and can be dropped by various enemies.

Spicy Bananas (Japanese: , Hotto Banana) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they taste disgustingly when eaten raw and are cultivated on Mechonis.

Soya Paste Shells are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by Entma Kings and Barbaric Sitri. No one has them available for trade. According to their description, they are shells with a soya paste flavour and the Chilkins use them to flavour sauces. Two are required for Cook-Off Showdown!.

The Sororal Statues (Japanese: , Gankutsu no Shimai-zō) are a landmark in . They are located in Satorl Marsh, on the east side of the map. While on the map it appears that the Statue Summit is easy to get to from here, the party must actually climb the statues, using vines growing on the walls in certain places. A Heart-to-Heart — "High Entia History" — is located here.
Soil Armour is medium torso armour in . It can be dropped by Leg Arduns and the Violent Andante.

The Soter Ruins (Japanese: , Sōtēru Iseki) is a location in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, southeast of the Glowing Obelisk landmark. The Indomitable Daulton, a Unique Monster, along with some other high level enemies, can be found in this area.
Soil Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various Armus on Bionis' Leg.

Speedy Ramshyde (Japanese: , Hayawaza no Ramushaido) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 10 at Cliff Lake in Colony 9, accompanied by two Junk Bunnits. It attacks on sight.
Soil Boots are medium feet armour in . They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Romantic Notions of a Boy, and can be dropped by some Arachnos and Krabbles.
Speed Boosters are Mechonis boosters in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Speed Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Speed Frames are Mechonis frames in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought at Hidden Village Shop 1 on the Fallen Arm.

Speed Goggles (Japanese: , Supīdo Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the basic Speed set for Fiora, along with the Speed Frame, Speed Arms, and Speed Boosters. Speed Goggles can only be obtained by purchasing them from Shop 1 in the Hidden Machina Village.

Solid Krabbles (Japanese: , Soriddo Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at Hazzai Cape in Colony 9 at night. They are level 35 and will attack on sight. They can drop Krabble Artwork, which is required for Désirée's Apology.
Speed II Goggles (Japanese: , Supīdo II Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Speed II set, along with the Speed II Frame, Speed II Arms, and Speed II Boosters.

Speed III Goggles (Japanese: , Supīdo III Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Speed III set for Fiora, along with the Speed III Frame, Speed III Arms, and Speed III Booster. Speed III Goggles can only be obtained by purchasing them from various shops.
Speed IV Goggles (Japanese: , Supīdo IV Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Speed V Goggles (Japanese: , Supīdo V Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Speed V set, along with the Speed V Frame, Speed V Arms, and Speed V Booster.
Soil Gear (Japanese: , Soiru Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Romantic Notions of a Girl.
Speed II Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Sparrow Blades (Japanese: , Suzume Sōken) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora, and can only be aquired from one shop, on the Fallen Arm.

The Soltnar Staff (Japanese: , Shimai Tsue Sorutana) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff and is usable by Melia. They can be acquired by purchasing them at the Syrath Lighthouse Shop at Eryth Sea for 21,600 G.

The Spinal Nerve Tower (Japanese: , Sekizui Shinkei Tawā) is a landmark in . It is located in the lower level of the Bionis' Interior. It is the first landmark the party discovers upon leaving the First Lung, being located just east of it. It is a junction of three different pathways; the east one leads to the Vein Crossroad, while the south one leads to a dead-end with an Ether Crystal deposit. A Heart-to-Heart - "Fiora's Body" - is located here.

Soul Read is an Art in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is used by Telethia, giving them the aura "Soul Read". The Telethia reads the party's minds, causing physical arts and auto-attacks to miss. This can be nullified by using Melia's Mind Blast, inflicting Aura Seal by using Monado Purge or inflicting Daze to the enemy. According to the in-battle tool tip, the Soul Read aura enables most physical attacks to be evaded.
Soothed Aglovale (Japanese: , Ando no Agurovare) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found near the Legislative District in Agniratha. It spawns grouped with two M87/GRANDs.

Solid Konev (Japanese: , Kenrōna Kōnefu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 10 at the south side of the Spring of Grief on the ground floor of Tephra Cave at night. It is slightly larger than the other krabble a few feet away.
Spike Defence (Japanese: , Supaiku Bōgyo) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that reduces the amount of Spike damage taken. __TOC__

Soft Hoxes (Japanese: , Sofuto Hoggusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Hox family, and can be found at level 17 in Colony 6 along the path between the Watchpoint Junction and the main gate, and along the Splintered Path before the events at Mechonis Core. Defeating six of them is required to complete the quest Safety First given by Daza in Colony 6.
Spear Break (Japanese: , Supiabureiku) is one of Melia's physical arts in and . It may knock back and inflict Slow to enemies that are hit.

Speed Shift (Japanese: , Supīdo Shifuto) is one of Fiora's arts in . Upon activation of this aura, the haste buff is activated and Double Attack rate is increased by 25% at the cost of 25% Physical Defence.
Speed IV Boosters are Mechonis boosters in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available from a shop in Colony 6.
Speed II Boosters are Mechonis boosters in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Speed III Boosters are Mechonis boosters in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Speed V Boosters are Mechonis boosters in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available as a reward from one quest.
Speed V Frames are Mechonis frames in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available as a reward for one quest.
Speed IV Frames are Mechonis frames in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available from a shop in Colony 6.
Speed III Frames are Mechonis frames in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available from two shops.
Speed II Frames are Mechonis frames in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Speed V Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are a part of the Speed V Armour Set, along with the Speed V Goggles, Speed V Booster, and Speed V Frame. They are only available as a quest reward for one quest.
Speed IV Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only available from a shop in Colony 6.
Speed III Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Spear Blade (Japanese: , Supia Burēdo) is one of Fiora's physical arts in . The damage is tripled when used against a Toppled enemy.

Sonicia Gogols (Japanese: , Sonishia Gogōru) are enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 96 in Tephra Cave, at the landmark Heavenly Window. They can drop the Gogol Horns needed for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Spear Tirkins are enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found from level 14-16 south of Gaur Plain or at Tirkin Headquarters on Bionis' Leg. They can drop the Tirkin Crests needed for Material Quest 2.

Soaring Tempest (Japanese: , Senjintenshō) is one of Dunban's physical arts in . Dunban leaps up and spins, inflicting damage to any nearby enemies. It is his only physical art capable of hitting multiple enemies. Each hit fills 10% of his Talent Gauge.

The Spanner is a Key Item in . Recovering it for a resident is the object of Search Quest 4 in Colony 9, and it can be found on the upper floor in the northwest corner of the Commercial District near the Gem Man's Stall.

The Spent Fuel Tank (Japanese: , Haiki Nenryō Tanku) is a location in . It is located on the first basement floor of Mechonis Field, south of 1st Lift - B1F. It is surrounded by an Ether sea that damages the party. One side of the tank holds spent fuel, which is not damaging and is safe to land in. It is separate from the main complex, and can only be reached by jumping from the first floor or higher floors, due to the surrounding ether sea. One method of reaching it is to go to the spiral cylinder on the east side of the 1F map. Instead of proceeding up the ramp on the cylinder, go to the second cog-like structure on the floor pointing out east southeast and, looking down so that the jump i
Special Bunnit Irons are rare materials in . They are dropped by various Bunnits, or can be traded for.

Soul Voices are game mechanics in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are useful tools for the team with various effects, such as Hit Points recovery. If a character gives advice, it can be considered and the effects will be earned. The advice appears as a colored text box above the related character, its color varying depending on the request of the character; a request for a Ranged attack will always be marked with a yellow text box, for example. The Arts that will operate the Soul Voice will begin to glow on the player's Arts palette. While the Soul Voices and effects of other characters are preset and cannot be changed, Cross's sixteen Soul Voices can be customized. However, twelve Soul Voices,
So Close, Yet So Far (Japanese: , Chikakute Tōi Kyori) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Audience Chamber in Alcamoth, between Shulk and Melia at purple affinity.
Sonar Lemons (Japanese: , Sonāremon) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia around Janpath Lake. Three are needed for Setting Forth.
The Special Mixer is a Key Item in . It is made by Shulk during Making a Mixer, and must be delivered to Rono to complete the quest.

Sorrow (悲しみ) is an Event Track in and , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 10 of disc 1 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is a sad theme that is heard in the following cutscenes: * Flashback to Dunban's words to Shulk as he's being carried in a stretcher after the Battle of Sword Valley * Day after Mechon raid on Colony 9 * Reyn saves Otharon from falling into ether river at the Central Pit - Base Level * Alvis' Telethia fights off the Mechon on Freight Road, prompting Metal Face to retreat * Dickson discusses Shulk's parents with him while making camp at the Glowing Obelisk in Satorl Marsh * The party deliberates in Whitewing Palace after discovering Fiora
Soldier Grexes (Japanese: , Torūpā Rupusu, Trooper Lupus) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family, and can be found at level 17-20 in Oblivia, near FN Site 302.

So nah, so fern is a track in , composed by and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano with vocals provided by Mika Kobayashi, and lyrics written by Rie. It is track 14 of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. It is heard in Chapter 9 and in Chapter 12, during two specific cutscenes which both feature Lao. * Chapter 9: When Lao is hospitalized in the Mimeosome Maintenance Center. * Chapter 12: Before the final boss battle in the Lifehold Core, when Luxaar and Lao fall into the protoplasm and undergo transformation. In the , this song also plays when Al and the Ares Prime are freed from Void's grasp after the first phase of the final battle.
The South Janpath BC (Japanese: , Janpasu-ko Nanbu BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, south of Janpath Lake and northeast of Seaswept Ridge.
The South Janpath Plain (Japanese: , Janpasu-ko no Minami Heigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, southeast of Janpath Lake.

Spear Insidias (Japanese: , Supiā Parako) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family, and can be found at level 12-14 near FN Site 219, Sunlit Spring, or at Goblin's Narrow in Noctilum. Three of them must be defeating during Arms Testers Wanted.

Soil Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Soiru Tapenta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Tectinsulas and can be found at level 18-20 at River Isle or in the eastern parts of Aaroy Plain in Oblivia. They can drop the Topaz Wine needed for Mystery Man.
The South Coast (Japanese: , Sausu Kōsuto) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, southeast of Barbarich Desert, and as the name suggests consists mainly of a beach.
South Silent Sandsea (Japanese: , Otonashi no Sakai Nanbu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, north of North Ciel Sandsea and south of North Silent Sandsea.
Spear Pugiliths (Japanese: , Supia Berudero) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Pugilith machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at level 41 at Milligan Supply Base in Oblivia.

Spear Puges (Japanese: , Supia Berude) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 45-47 in Primordia, notably on the Lesser Gemini Bridge and within the Bedrock Hold.

Spinel Forfexes (Japanese: , Supineru Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 11-14 at Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum, particularly the northeast coast.
South Hardheart Canyon (Japanese: , Mujō no Keikoku Nanbu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, south of Hardheart Canyon. It must be visited during Brotherly Love.

Sparrow Adseculas (Japanese: , Suparou Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 29-30 (large-sized) north of FN Site 408 in Sylvalum's Lake Ciel, and level 23-24 (small-sized) near Cleansing Spring. Four of them must be defeated to complete Adsecula Extermination, although only the large ones are accepted for the mission.
Soma Scirpos (Japanese: , Sōma Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family, and can be found at level 8 west of Cascade Isle in Noctilum.
Spiral Horn is one of many Melee Arts in . It deals weapon damage and inflicts Physical Res Down.
The South Ciel Sandsea (Japanese: , Shieru-ko no Nanbu Sakai) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, northwest of the Needle Rock Sandsea and just south of Lake Ciel.

The Southern Searoad (Japanese: , Minami no Kaiendō) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in eastern Sylvalum, near the base of Delusians South Summit and north of the Cleansing Spring.
Solan (English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

Sona Herbs (Japanese: , Sonahābu) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia near Northpointe Beach. They seem to spawn 2-4 at a time. Three of them are needed during The Fashionista.

The Soldier Chimeras (Japanese: , Sorujā Kimaera) are ten Story Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Chimeras, and are fought between the battles between Vita and the final boss at level 48. They may also be summoned by the final boss at level 41-50. They are components of the Lifehold Core's built-in security system.

South Ant's Nest (Japanese: , Anto Nesuto Nanbu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a small cave located in Oblivia, near the Ant's Nest and North Ant's Nest on the lip of the Yawning Giant, with only one cavern and no enemies within it. There is, however, one mechanical Treasure Box.
Spiked Pomegranates (Japanese: , Zazakuro) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular near the Primeval Meadow.
Sour Plums (Japanese: , Supaume) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Socha Guavas (Japanese: , Ncha Guaba) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Seven are needed for the mission Gaga for Guavas.
Spine-O-Correctors (Japanese: , Senaoshi Mashīn) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.
Snowy Angelhairs (Japanese: , Howaito Paseran) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found rarely in Sylvalum southern coastal near FN Site 403 and in Lake Ciel.

Sorcerer Papils (Japanese: , Sōsarā Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 11-12 at Seabird's Beak (near Blaudolch, the Chalcedony's spawn point) in Sylvalum at daytime. Five of them must be defeated during Papil Punisher.
Solar Wind Converters (Japanese: , Kōseifū Tenkan Debaisu) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros, inside the Ganglion Weapons Hangar.
Spatial Control Jointers (Japanese: , Kūkan Seigyo Jointā) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.
Sonic Blattas (Japanese: , Sonikku Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 51-54 in Cauldros, southeast of FN Site 509.
South Cinderdunes (Japanese: , Minami no Kaijin Sakyū) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, to the west of North Ciel Sandsea and South Silent Sandsea.
Sphinxes (Japanese: , Ryuosu) are quadrupedal fire-breathing lion-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

Spaniel, the Obedient (Japanese: , Jūjun naru Supanieru) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Caro family. It can be found at level 40 at O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins in Cauldros at any time except late night. It is accompanied by Duran, the Draconian and a pair of Legion Caro, all of which are kindred enemies.

Sorrowful Saltats (Japanese: , Sorou Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 35-37 west of King's Falls in Oblivia, occasionally replacing Mystic Saltats in the small group.

Solid Puges (Japanese: , Soriddo Berude) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros, north of FN Site 507 or west of FN Site 508.
Soft Cat Ears are casual head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They have the same appearance on all characters.
Spicy Sacrifole Pollen is a common material in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Sacrifoles. Three units are required for Sparking a Smile (B route).
Sostenasa (Japanese: , Sosutenasa) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is located in the Hangar in the Administrative District.
Soothing Angel Wings are a casual head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Another pair of wings, the Relaxing Angel Wings, are available in white.

Soldier of the Harriers (Japanese: , Avaranchi no Hei, Soldier of Avalanche) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be received near the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles

Sparking a Smile (Japanese: , Kirakira no Hate, Glittering End) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Ngogo at the Nopon Bazaar in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.

The Soghu Caladar (Japanese: , De Sogu) is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the Caladar Skell piloted by De Soghu, fought at level 40 at the North Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum during Leaving the Nest.

Spending Time is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located two segments north and one segment northeast of West Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles between Celica and Cross in the morning.

Soldier Insidias (Japanese: , Sorujā Parako) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family, and are fought at level 40 at Fukai Pass in Noctilum during Climbing the Ladder. They drop no treasure.
Special Delivery (Japanese: , Himitsu no Todokemono, Secret Delivery) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Zazazan at the Cauldros Gate at the entrance to Cauldros.
The Solar Starship Map is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Obtaining it is required during Proficiency Exam 4, it can be found at Humdrum Peaks in Noctilum.
Spiked Tail Fins are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Lophids.

The Speed Mod Custom Skell (Japanese: , Suwifutokasutamu) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Human-Made Skell fought at level 30 in Oblivia's Great Washington Isle during the Normal Mission Professor B's Return.

Sparkling Blue Gems are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from blue Levitath, or for 178 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Artful Execution Surge augments.

Sparkling Purple Gems are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from purple Levitath, or for 178 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX High Danger Surge augments.

Sparkling Red Gems are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from red Levitath, or for 178 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Incapacitation Surge augments.
Sphinx A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black sphinx variant. It can be obtained from Tainted Sphinx in Noctilum, a boss fought during Chapter 6.
Sphinx B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a brown sphinx variant. It can be obtained at daytime from Durvin, the Perceptive in Primordia or Feliciano, the All-Seeing in Oblivia.

Spatha Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Meredith & Co. Longsword. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission New Frontier. The Spatha weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Spatha * Iron Spatha * Carbide Spatha * Cermet Spatha * Chrome Spatha * Chromoly Spatha * Cobalt Spatha * Titanium Spatha * Ceramic Spatha * Diamond Spatha

Spear Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Javelin. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Xenotech category of the Oblivia Collectopedia. The Spear weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Spear * Iron Spear * Carbide Spear * Cermet Spear * Chrome Spear * Chromoly Spear * Cobalt Spear * Titanium Spear * Ceramic Spear * Diamond Spear

Spear II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Javelin. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Insects category of the Sylvalum Collectopedia. The Spear II weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Spear II * Iron Spear II * Carbide Spear II * Cermet Spear II * Chrome Spear II * Chromoly Spear II * Cobalt Spear II * Titanium Spear II * Ceramic Spear II * Diamond Spear II

Spider Nest is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.5, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eight Marnucks. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Sphere Speculation is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.8, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting six Enhanced Search Zigs. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Soft Touch is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance to not dispel the Sleep debuff when attacking.
SpecUp.HP.Max is a Skell armor stat augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell Hit Points by 100 to 1500. It is the Skell equivalent of Max HP Up.

Special Bonuses are Consumable Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be received as Division Rewards for Division activities. They can be sold for 10,000 Credits via the Inventory, and do not serve any other purpose.

Soldier Assault Rifles are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Assault Rifles. They can only be obtained from the Shop Terminal on Armory Alley for 4,500 Credits. A Soldier Assault Rifle must be purchased as an objective for the Affinity Mission Boot Camp. It must then be used to complete Elma's Task A, Elma's Task B, and Elma's Task C.
is a Skell frame fuel augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases fuel efficiency by 5% to 100% when fighting in a Skell.
is a Skell frame fuel augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases fuel recovery by 1 to 20 units per 10 seconds when a Skell is parked.
SpecUp.FUEL-BIND is a Skell frame fuel augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases fuel recovery by 1 to 20 units per second when a Skell is binding an enemy.
is a Skell frame fuel augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It recovers 50 to 250 fuel when activating Overdrive.
SpecUp.APP-HP is a skell armor stat augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases maximum HP for the appendage it is equipped to by 50 to 1000.
SpecUp.EVA is a Skell armor stat augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell evasion by 5 to 25. It is the Skell equivalent of Evasion Up.
SpecUp.PHYS-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell physical resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Physical Res Up.
SpecUp.BEAM-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell beam resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Beam Res Up.
SpecUp.ELEC-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell electric resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Electric Res Up.
SpecUp.THERM-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell thermal resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Thermal Res Up.
SpecUp.ETHER-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell ether resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Ether Res Up,
SpecUp.GRAV-RES is a skell armor attribute resistance augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell gravity resistance by 1 to 20. The ground equivalent is Gravity Res Up.
Spike.EVA is a Skell armor special augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants a 1% to 20% chance of evading spike damage when in a Skell. The ground equivalent is Antispike.
SpecUp.M-ACC is a Skell weapon stat augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell melee accuracy by 5 to 100. It is the Skell equivalent of Melee Accuracy Up.
SpecUp.R-ACC is a Skell weapon stat augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell ranged accuracy by 5 to 100. It is the Skell equivalent of Ranged Accuracy Up.
SpecUp.M-ATK is a Skell weapon weapon stat Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell melee attack by 5 to 100. It is the Skell equivalent of Melee Attack Up.
SpecUp.R-ATK is a Skell weapon stat Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell ranged attack by 5 to 100. It is the Skell equivalent of Ranged Attack Up.
SpecUp.PTL is a Skell weapon stat Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell Potential by 5 to 100. It is the Skell equivalent of Potential Up.

Soothing Angel Halos are casual head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It has the same appearance on all characters, and shares this appearance with the Warm Angel Halo and Supreme Angel Halo. It can only be obtained from a Treasure Box in Oblivia (Biological level 3) just south of Victory Rock.
Spinning Cutter (Japanese: , Guruguru kattā) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Tora's arts when using a Drill Shield and has an area of effect damage.
Spin of Bravery (Japanese: , Bureibusupin; lit. Brave Spin) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using Twin Rings.

Solitary Block #1 (Japanese: , Dai-ichi Dokubō Kukaku) is a location in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province along a corridor from the Engine Room, and can be reached by breaking through a vent from the Port-side Walkway. There are two Treasure Troves here.

Solitary Block #2 (Japanese: , Dai-ni Dokubō Kukaku) is a location in . It is located aboard the Titan Battleship in Gormott Province, just beyond the Sickbay. This is where Nia is initially held captive by the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Soulcrown Summit (Japanese: , Tamashii no Itadaki) is a landmark in . It is located in the Head of Uraya, beyond Lake Varna. Wulfric's Core Crystal is obtained here. There are no enemies here except the initial story-exclusive Boss.
The Soprac Old Market (Japanese: , Sopurakku Kyūshōtengai) is a Location in . It is located in Theosoir of the Kingdom of Tantal. There are multiple shops located here.

Sparklesugars are Dessert Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Honeycomb Sweets in the Argentum Trade Guild. Ten are required, two per batch of cookies, to prepare the Whelzaman Cookie recipe during Theory and Praxis. One can be used to prepare a ration needed for the quest The Supply Situation.
Sparkly Snow Perfumes are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Cosmetipolitan in Torigoth of the Gormott Province. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Finch and Theory.
The Soniarus Deeds are Store Deeds in . They can be purchased from Soniarus Music in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Snowflake Scarves are Textile Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Neuromin Textiles in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Sour-Spark-on-a-Sticks are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Sadecott Groceries in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.

Snowy Dudleya Gelées are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased at the Lectica Vegetables run by Lucisthenes in the Kingdom of Tantal's Theosoir. They can also be purchased for 2,520 G from the Pouch Item Emporium in the Land of Challenge after collecting the Nopon Invitation, Pt. 2 on Version 1.5.2 or later.
Snowflake-Weave Soles are Textile Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Boldarde Textiles in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Soniarus Music is a shop in . It is run by Tros and can be found in Torigoth in the Gormott Province. It is specialized in Instruments.

Sovereigns (Japanese: , Roiyaru) refer to various enemies in . They are high-tech robots that serve as the World Tree's automated defense systems and common enemies, although some can also be found in the Land of Morytha. Although they share the "Sovereign" title, they come in a number of distinct models. Sentries are non-offensive poles, they can draw the attention of Sovereigns. A few named runners or scouts are used as scouts but this term can be used for other species.
Spinning Elbow (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Greataxe. When used, Zeke steps back and thrusts his greataxe then his elbow forward.

Soul-Eater Stanley (Japanese: , Tamagurai no Furan) is a Unique Monster in . He is a member of the Guldo family and can be found at level 56 to the east of the Collapsed Roadway in the Land of Morytha. He must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 4 Ascension Blade and Praxis's level 5 Foam Blast Blade Specials.
Speedy Sword (Japanese: , Gyungyun sōdo) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Tora's arts when using a Variable Saber. Tora spins around while cutting with the saber.

Spellbinder Billy (Japanese: , Mahōtsukai no Birī) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Peng family, and can be found at level 46 along the Genbu Drifts in the Kingdom of Tantal. It only appears during Snowy weather.

Soothsayer Gerald (Japanese: , Shinshi no Akutaiōn) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Ellook family, and can be found at level 78 at Loska's Gap in the Kingdom of Uraya. Field Skills must be used to create an ice bridge to reach him. Soothsayer Gerald only appears when the weather is falling blossom petals, which only happens at night (between 19:00 and 7:00). It must be defeated to unlock T-elos's level 5 T-SKYLLA.
